newsitem.title: USA: Two Democrats vie for US House budget panel post.
newsitem.headline: Two Democrats vie for US House budget panel post.

text.p: Two Democrats are vying for the party's senior position on the House Budget Committee being vacated by former chairman Martin Sabo of Minnesota. Six-term Rep. Louise Slaughter, D-New York, an opponent of the balanced budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution, and eight-term Rep. John Spratt of South Carolina, who voted for the budget amendment in the last session, both announced they will seek the post.
Democrats will vote on the choice of ranking committee members Wednesday and the Budget Committee race is one of only two in contention.
There is a three-way race for Democratic leader of the House Banking Committee.

Slaughter has served three terms on the Budget Committee and is now the third most senior Democratic member of the panel. She is the only Democratic woman in the House in line to hold a committee leadership post. Sabo, the senior Democrat since Republicans won control of the House in 1994, decided to leave the panel as did the second ranking member, Charles Stenholm of Texas. Stenholm is in line to take over the Agriculture Committee's ranking minority post.

In a letter to House Democrats, Slaughter stressed her commitment to balancing the budget by the year 2002, but added that cuts should not damage education or infrastructure and the elderly and children should be protected.
Spratt challenged Sabo for the chairmanship in 1991 but House Democrats rejected him by 37 votes.

"We have to produce a budget resolution that wipes out the deficit over five years without wiping out programs we support like Medicare, Medicaid, and education. It is important that we balance the budget, but it is equally important how we balance it," he wrote.
